subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Spinal dysraphism: folate, myelomeningocele, tethered cord and sinus

steps.say: Folate is preventing most neural tube defects when started a month before conception. High-risk mothers are receiving four milligrams daily and routine mothers zero point four. Closure is happening in the first month of pregnancy.
steps.tx: Periconceptional **folic acid** prevents most neural tube defects: 4 mg dose daily for high-risk and 0.4 mg for routine mothers, started at least a month before conception. High risk means prior affected child, epilepsy drugs, diabetes or obesity. Closure completes by day 28, often before pregnancy is known.

steps.say: Myelomeningocele is exposing the placode through open skin and dura in the low spine. Cerebrospinal fluid is leaking while Chiari two is pulling the hindbrain down. Hydrocephalus with leg, bowel and bladder deficits is following.
steps.tx: Myelomeningocele exposes the **placode** through defective skin and dura in the lumbosacral spine, with CSF leak guaranteeing Chiari II, hydrocephalus and orthopaedic and bladder deficits. The placode is the open cord itself, not a covering. Every case gets head imaging and bladder assessment.

vis.alt: Sagittal diagrams comparing normal posterior fossa with Chiari I tonsillar descent and Chiari II with brainstem descent and syrinx.
vis.caption: Chiari II with hindbrain descent and syrinx accompanies myelomeningocele. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Prenatal repair before twenty-six weeks is halving shunt need and improving leg function. Two setbacks are tempering the gain: prematurity and uterine dehiscence. Selection is strict and counselling is detailed.
steps.tx: The **MOMS trial** proved prenatal repair before 26 weeks halves shunt need and improves motor outcomes versus postnatal repair, at the price of 2 setbacks: prematurity and uterine dehiscence. Mothers accept preterm birth risk for the child gain. Centres with fetal surgery programs offer it.

steps.say: Postnatal closure is happening within forty-eight hours with placode tubularisation inside. Dura and skin are closed watertight to block meningitis. Ventricles are shunted when they are enlarging afterwards.
steps.tx: Postnatal **48 hour closure** with placode tubularisation, dural closure and skin cover prevents meningitis, followed by shunting when ventricles enlarge. The placode is folded into a tube, never excised. Delay invites ventriculitis that ruins candidacy for shunting. Two surgeons often work together, one on cord and one on cover.

vis.alt: Spinal dysraphism variants with myelomeningocele placode herniation, fetal ultrasound with lemon and banana signs and cranial signs.
vis.caption: Occulta, meningocele and myelomeningocele with placode, ultrasound signs and Chiari II markers. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A low conus with a thick filum is tethering the cord in a growing child. Back pain with foot deformity, scoliosis or new incontinence is revealing the stretch. Imaging is confirming conus below L2.
steps.tx: Tethered cord holds the **conus below L2** with a thickened filum thicker than 2 mm, presenting with back pain, foot deformity, scoliosis and new incontinence in a growing child. Growth spurts unmask the tether. Urodynamics documents the bladder cost. Cutaneous markers often overlie the level.

steps.say: Sectioning the filum through a small opening is releasing the cord with minimal exposure. Fatty lumps with intact skin are untethered before deficits are appearing. Prophylaxis is beating repair after damage.
steps.tx: Detethering by **filum section** through a limited laminotomy frees the cord, while lipomyelomeningocele with intact skin gets prophylactic detethering before deficits appear. Fatty stalks tether as the spine grows. Early release preserves bladder and feet. Intraoperative monitoring guards motor roots.

steps.say: A bony spur is splitting the cord into two hemicords that are tethering separately. Spur resection with dural rebuilding is freeing both halves. Detethering is completing the operation.
steps.tx: Split cord malformation with a **bony spur** dividing the cord into 2 hemicords needs spur resection with dural reconstruction plus detethering, since either half tethers growth. Two dural tubes may need merging into one. Imaging defines spur level before cutting.

steps.say: Midline pits with hair or discharge are marking dermal sinus tracts to the thecal sac. Complete excision is removing the whole tract to block dermoids and meningitis. Retained epithelium is seeding trouble years later.
steps.tx: Congenital **dermal sinus** tracts from failed dysjunction connect skin pits to the thecal sac and need complete tract excision, because retained epithelium seeds dermoids and meningitis. Hairy pits with discharge are the surface clue. MRI traces the tract before surgery.
